Planned concept · no zomes exist on the land yet

Zome Range

Zome Build Plan

Five zome sizes planned for Portal.Place in Clearwater, BC, Canada, each modelled from its own plan, with 30 floor plans and 20 transparent versions. Choose what to build, and the page becomes the plan.

These are not scaled copies. Strut length, panel slope, row count and doorway all come from each plan. The Acorn carries an extra row past its widest ring, the 5 m is steeper than the 6 m, and the 7.5 and 9 m have a gable dormer that the smaller ones can’t carry. Every drawing and 3D interior comes from the same data, and each layout had to pass a check: everything inside the floor, clear of the sloped walls at its own height, nothing overlapping, doors free to swing, head height where you need to stand.

Only the zomes and items chosen for this build. Figures are estimates in Canadian dollars, not quotes.

All-in costs

With volunteers building and leading the site, the clad 5 to 9 m layouts run from about $37,000 to about $135,000 each. Volunteer hours are in the last two columns and are not in the subtotal.

Small zomes cost more per square metre. The Acorn Sauna runs about $5,900/m² and the 9 m Three-Bedroom Home about $2,400/m². Power, engineering and site work barely shrink with size.

A bathroom adds about $15,000 to $20,000. That counts the plumber, the water and sewer line, fixtures, contingency and tax. Plumbing is the biggest single decision in most layouts.

Clear zomes are cheaper to enclose, not always to finish. Polycarbonate saves about 40 to 50% of the materials cost, but spa equipment takes the 7.5 and 9 m halls back over $110,000.

Budget options

QtyLayoutSizeMaterialsFurniture, fit-outPro servicesDelivery, permits, contingency, taxEachLikely rangeVolunteer hoursVolunteer value

Not in these numbers

  • New septic, unless added above. Existing infrastructure has capacity for several more dwellings, so each plumbed layout is priced as a tie-in. Beyond that, a shared system runs $22,000 to $36,000 conventional, or $45,000 to $85,000+ advanced.
  • Volunteer food, lodging, tools and training. Roads, landscaping, and any new power or water capacity beyond a 50 m run.
  • Public-use code upgrades, flagged on those layouts. Café and dining kitchens are priced as simple kitchens, without commercial hoods.
  • Year-round performance. Clad layouts have R-12 in the panels and baseboards or a stove. BC Energy Step Code testing or deeper insulation would add cost.

How this is priced

  • Quantities come from each Trillium materials list, plus panel area, seam length and item counts from each model.
  • The site lead is a volunteer by default, which relies on someone experienced being available for the whole build.
  • Range: materials −12% to +20%, services −20% to +40%, contingency 10% to 20%.
  • About 40% of the unit prices are published listings. The rest are allowances, mostly windows, site work, trades scope and specialty items. Local quotes replace these next.
  • Online prices aren’t Clearwater shelf prices, and the Home Depot listings read from an Ontario store.
  • Permit fees assume the Thompson-Nicola Regional District. No permits are in place for this build-out.

Where the plan set disagrees with itself

  • The cover says 2896 mm tall. The frame plus base comes to 2.77 m. The other 130 mm isn’t explained; it may be the deck.
  • The component list says 17 z3 panels and 9 z4. The geometry says the sixth row has to be the z4 shape, so it should be the other way round. Same total area, but cut counts change. The model follows the geometry.
  • It lists 13 special panels but itemises 15. The z5 miter prints 15° where its own dimensions give 16°.

Worked out from the plans

  • The door sits 0.46 m behind the base line. That comes from the printed door-card width and the printed 935 mm gap at the base.

Doorway

Where the plan set disagrees with itself

  • The z4 half panel prints 1686 mm sides. That is the 9 m zome’s strut, pasted in; it should be 1423 mm.
  • Roof panel C’s bottom edge is 537 mm on the imperial sheet and 594 mm on the metric one. 537 mm is the plausible one.
  • No door opening is printed, only a 1905 mm header and 2032 mm trimmers, so those are used as the opening.

Worked out from the plans

  • The front wall sits 590 mm ahead of the base corners, read from the roof panel width. The eave ties to ring 4, which matches the printed wall height to within 30 mm.

Doorway

  • Gable dormer (“Fancy” doorway)

30′ · 9 m

9 m Zome

The largest. Trillium ships two complete doorways for it: a gable dormer (“Fancy”) and a shed-roof awning (“Basic”). Both modelled.

Strut length
1686 mm
Panel rows
5 rows + half base
Panel slope
33.1° generator
Widest
9.32 m plan 9.30
Height
5.76 m above its floor plan 6.04
Floor

non-beveled

Gable dormer (“Fancy”)

Shed awning (“Basic”)

Where the plan set disagrees with itself

  • Two complete doorways are published with different panel counts (44 and 46 regular). They are alternatives; don’t add them together. Both are modelled.
  • The model is 5.92 m with a deck against 6.045 m printed, 125 mm short with nothing to account for it. Widest (9.32 vs 9.30 m) and base (8.85 m) agree.
  • The eighth deck joist prints 586 mm; the series says 686 mm.

Worked out from the plans

  • No door size is printed. The 1905 mm Basic header and the 2126 mm Fancy header are used as the openings.
  • The Basic doorway’s front sits 1219 mm ahead of ring 3, taken from the side wall panels.

Doorway

  • Gable dormer (“Fancy” doorway)
  • Shed-roof awning (“Basic” doorway)

Before anyone builds from this

  • These are layouts and concept renders, not engineered drawings. Lofts, the big glass spans and snow load on clear panels all need an engineer, and no permits are in place.
  • Floor height is an assumption: 350 mm above ground on piers, with a 2-step entry. It moves to suit each site.
  • Single-wall polycarbonate won’t hold much heat, so the glass rooms are three-season unless a double-walled sheet is used. Hot tubs and spas also need venting, drainage and water.
  • Where the plans contradict themselves, the model follows the geometry and the conflict is listed under each size. Check those before cutting anything.

Zome geometry is based on plans by Trillium Domes, © Golden Trillium Geodesics LLC. Layouts, models and estimates by Portal.Place. Concept planning document. Figures are estimates, not quotes.
